📖 Executive Summary - Batch Processing Architecture

Year-end rollover processing is the most resource-intensive operation in the RA Domain, orchestrating balance rollovers for up to 50,000 accounts annually while maintaining RegulatoryAgency compliance. The V2 batch architecture reduced processing time from 90+ minutes to 15-20 minutes—an 85% performance improvement—enabling real-time year-end operations.

This dashboard details the batch processing implementation: parallel workers, pre-fetch optimization, feature flag rollout strategy, and transactional integrity mechanisms that transformed a sequential bottleneck into a horizontally-scalable operation.

🚀 V2 Batch Processing Transformation

The Performance Challenge

The original V1 architecture processed accounts sequentially—one at a time—resulting in 90+ minute execution times during year-end operations. This created operational risk: if year-end processing started December 31st at 11:00 PM, it wouldn't complete until January 1st at 12:30 AM, delaying account availability and triggering customer support escalations.

The V1 implementation also exhibited the N+1 query anti-pattern: for each account, the system made separate database calls to retrieve plan configuration, rollover settings, and organization rules. Processing 26,000 accounts generated 104,000+ database queries, overwhelming database connection pools and causing timeout failures.

The V2 Solution: Parallel Batching

The refactored V2 architecture partitions 50,000 accounts into 1,000-record batches, processing 10 batches concurrently using parallel workers. Each worker operates independently, eliminating sequential bottlenecks and enabling horizontal scaling.

Pre-fetch optimization loads all required data (plans, rollover settings, organization configurations) in a single database query per batch. Instead of 104,000+ queries, V2 executes ~50 queries total—a 95% reduction in database roundtrips. This eliminates connection pool exhaustion and reduces database CPU load by 80%.

Result: 26,000 accounts processed in 15-20 minutes (85% faster than V1), with throughput capacity of 26,000 accounts/minute at peak. The system now completes year-end processing in time for midnight customer portal availability, eliminating operational risk.

Architecture Components

Batch Size (1,000 accounts): Optimized through performance testing to balance memory consumption and throughput. Larger batches (5,000 accounts) caused out-of-memory errors, while smaller batches (100 accounts) increased overhead from transaction commits.

Concurrent Workers (10 parallel): Matches database connection pool size (10 connections) and CPU core count (12 cores, leaving 2 for system overhead). This configuration maximizes parallelism without triggering resource contention.

Pre-Fetch Strategy: Entity Framework's .Include() and .ThenInclude() methods load related entities (Account → Plan → RolloverSettings → Organization) in a single SQL JOIN query. This eliminates lazy-loading delays and N+1 query patterns.

Transactional Integrity: Each batch commits atomically—either all 1,000 accounts succeed, or the entire batch rolls back. This prevents partial updates that could corrupt financial data or violate audit requirements. Failed batches are logged with correlation IDs for manual investigation.

Feature Flag-Driven Rollout

The V2 architecture deployed via LaunchDarkly feature flags (SplitJobPerformanceV2 global flag), enabling gradual rollout without code changes. Initial deployment targeted 20% of employers for A/B testing, comparing V2 performance against V1 baselines.

Per-organization override capability allows instant rollback if issues emerge. During rollout, one organization encountered data validation errors (unrelated to batch processing). The engineering team disabled V2 for that organization via feature flag, investigated the issue (missing rollover settings), fixed the data, and re-enabled V2—all without production downtime.

Current status: V2 is globally active for 100% of employers. The feature flag remains enabled for emergency rollback capability, with plans to remove the flag after 6 months of stable production operation.

Horizontal Scaling Capacity

The batch processing architecture scales linearly with customer growth. Current configuration (10 workers, 1,000-record batches) processes 26,000 accounts/minute. Doubling workers to 20 would achieve 52,000 accounts/minute, enabling the platform to scale to 100,000+ accounts without architectural redesign.

Scaling limits: Database connection pool (current: 10 connections) and server CPU cores (current: 12 cores) constrain maximum parallelism. Increasing to 20 workers requires database connection pool expansion and vertical scaling (16-core servers). Cloud infrastructure (Azure SQL Elastic Pools) supports this scaling path.

✅ Business Impact: 85% faster year-end processing, 95% fewer database queries, zero operational incidents during 2024-2025 year-end rollover, horizontal scaling capacity to 100,000+ accounts. The V2 architecture transformed year-end operations from a high-risk bottleneck into a reliable, scalable operation.
